blocks.text: This page tracks the Whistler MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $1,359,000 for a typical home, little changed at −1.3% over twelve months.
Whistler benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Whistler home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $1,359,000 in October 2026. That is little changed at +0.6% on the month, up 4.4% over three months, up 5.3% over six months and little changed at −1.3% over the year. Over three years it is down 4.9%, and over five years down 4.1%.
The weakest one-year move in Whistler was for a townhouse homes at −5.4%; the strongest was a detached home at +2.2%.
The gap between a detached home ($2,646,200) and an apartment ($612,500) is $2,033,700, and a townhouse ($1,621,200) sits $1,008,700 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,068,600, Whistler is 27.2% above. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.2% against little changed at −1.3% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Whistler ranks 3 by all-home benchmark, with Bowen Island above it at $1,395,700 and North Vancouver below it at $1,281,400.

Detached homes in Whistler: benchmark $2,646,200, up 3.6% in a month, up 3.3% in three months, little changed at −0.7% in six months, up 2.2% in a year, up 5.4% in three years and little changed at +0.7% in five. That is 49.1% above the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,775,200).

Townhouse homes in Whistler: benchmark $1,621,200, down 4.4% in a month, down 2.3% in three months, little changed at −0.9% in six months, down 5.4% in a year, down 5.8% in three years and up 10.0% in five. That is 61.1% above the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,006,500).

Apartment homes in Whistler: benchmark $612,500, up 1.9% in a month, up 11.3% in three months, up 18.9% in six months, down 4.8% in a year, down 16.3% in three years and down 7.1% in five. That is 9.0% below the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($673,400).

blocks.source: Source: Greater Vancouver REALTORS® MLS® Home Price Index, October 2026 (released November 2, 2026).

blocks.text: In dollars, the typical Whistler home is worth about $17,900 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $1,376,900. By type, detached homes gained about $57,000, from $2,589,200 to $2,646,200, townhouses lost about $92,500, from $1,713,700 to $1,621,200, and apartments lost about $30,900, from $643,400 to $612,500 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $1,290,600 six months ago and near $1,429,000 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $68,400 above the six-month mark and about $70,000 below the three-year mark. Against Greater Vancouver, the Whistler benchmark is about $290,400 above the regional $1,068,600; a year earlier the difference was about $249,700 above.
The $1,359,000 Whistler figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for October 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Whistler?
faq.a: In October 2026, a typical Whistler home was $1,359,000, with detached at $2,646,200.

faq.q: Are Whistler home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Whistler is little changed at −1.3% over twelve months and up 4.4% over three months.
